description: Ready-made delivery views and snapshot commands layered on the complete core profile: a live line map, a delivery history page and tracker and forge snapshots, configured rather than coded. Merge recovery preserves source occurrence time separately from observation, with unknown timing left unknown. Views show stage-specific recorded times and compact cross-repository pull request identities. Native runless review reports use bounded observational capture and candidate-bound shared cards. Originating closure details are collapsed by default in shared review cards. Ready and merge hooks receive an exact runner-derived single or batch check mode without changing admission. The line map gains a plan chapter from an optional delivery-plan/1 input: which criteria are proven, from the record and producer evidence, what changed since approval, and what needs the engineer. The plan chapter also shows how the plan was approved, from an optional planReview: one line for its review rounds and outcome, and a folded review track and cards; approvals marked blocking raise a flag until they are done. A binding may let the lead choose a candidate's checks from its diff, recorded per reviewed head and voided by a new head; the record, results, views and stats name the lead's choice and reason, and without the option the provider selects as before. Delivery records can hold lane ownership, current story assignments, and temporary flakes scoped to a base commit and check. Authorized base merges can retain an aligned review through hand-off. Integration-base setup records its target and uses the integration checkout for delivery. Record writers are pinned by applied archive digest and changed through a parked lead transition. Integration-base moves preserve recorded commit ancestry and recover publication and applied-writer reconciliation once. A stopped base rerun is told from a failed one, a named repair lands first and alone through a queue its broken base stopped, and batch members define a check alike when what it runs is alike. A lens re-checks each finding it deferred earlier, and one it does not list as fixed stays deferred. A round card says when an approval carried deferrable notes. A base move that changed nothing a check reads, by the binding's own declaration, carries that check, and deliveries that merge into one base on a machine share one merge slot. The line map labels a carried check, a flaky base run and a peer's merge. A bounded data-only public snapshot reuses line-map payloads while excluding history, raw artifacts and local execution details. Optional owned hosted publishing collects coherent source cuts, reconciles fenced writer receipts and keeps credentials out of view data and children. Owned hosted publishing starts or adopts an independent generation-aware watcher, bounds terminal close publication to 30 seconds, retains pending terminal cuts for ten-minute retries and supports credential-free archive viewing with explicit archive retry. Credential-free terminal notifications reach an existing owner independently of lifecycle-lock contention and preserve one deadline per finished cut. Hosted publishing is qualified from exact built archive bytes in two independently configured adopters; the separately deployed viewer and its dependencies are excluded from workflow archives. The hosted page shows what the local live view shows, from the same record; a cut holding a configured secret's value or a credential-named field is refused with its code, which the retried status names, and a sibling's hosted link, which grants read access to that delivery, is left out as a credential. Workflows may consult an optional, read-only knowledge library after the repository's own solution notes, and report that it was not consulted when none is configured. Journal entries hold typed facts by registered kind with their causes and no sentence; a record in the older journal shape is refused and closes under the release that wrote it. A narrator tells the journal as a story of chapters, beats and setbacks that open and close. The views show the delivery's story at three depths. The hosted snapshot publishes each journal entry's identity and kind and a review round's counts, with no other facts, no link a fact names and no story, and refuses the earlier snapshot version. A candidate that adds or removes provenance outputs syncs over a base that only refreshed digests, taking the candidate's listing and regenerating; when both sides changed the listing it stops as before. Once a check of a lone candidate's run has failed, a new hand-off supersedes the rest of that run and any base re-run that follows, on the lead's acceptance, or on the hand-off itself when the delivery needs no acceptance; a batch run is never superseded. The acceptance journals check.superseded, and the queue then stops the checks it started, writes no verdict and never checks the old head again; lead-base-broken names the base broken before a re-run's verdict, with --repair naming another candidate or --self-repair making the failing story's next accepted head the repair; without either, a failed check re-runs on the base as before, and the line map says what a running re-run is for, when it should end and what the lead can do instead. A region claim may name its story, and the state tool refuses one naming a story the record doesn't hold; ownership.released, ownership.carried and ownership.carved record what a landing and a carve do to claims, and the queue's ownership check reports every path and hunk outside a lane's claims at once. When the record has region claims, the line map's Who's doing what chapter offers a Who holds which files view, closed by default, read from the record and lane-changes.json: each claimed file solid where its lane has changed it and hollow where it hasn't, each shared file split by its lanes' line stretches, and a shared file's reading with each lane's stretches, changes and changed functions; a lane whose branch can't be read is shown so, and with no region claims the page has no such view. A record with an integration target carries meta.integration with its base, target and remote; integration.merged, integration.suite, integration.requested and integration.landed record the step into the target, and a review.round under the delivery's own key carries the head it read. On a delivery with an integration target, the line map's headline reads in two beats naming the target, its drift and the catch-ups, the line runs on past the integration base through the target merged in, the suite, the review and the change request into the target, and a Before it rejoins ledger pins each proof to the head it was taken at and strikes one a newer head supersedes; a delivery without one renders as before. The local line map's corner names the checkout's git identity beside the theme switch, as an icon that shows it on a tap on a phone, and the hosted page never carries it; the files view stays hidden until a branch read lists a file or fails; and the kicker's start and close read as a person says them, on a short line with the run between. A per-machine ledger, shared by every repository on the machine, records each heavy run's claim on a capacity of slots and its measured cost; heavy commands claim and wait by default when the machine is full, an agent steps off a default with a recorded reason, and the Machine view shows who is using the machine.
